correctness.rationale: For n>=2 and -1/(n-1)<rho<1, the entrywise independent relative symmetric perturbation set is universally PD exactly when 0<=u<tau_n(rho). For a fixed test x the worst perturbation aligns signs of x, giving G-u S|G|S, so checking all sign vertices is sufficient and necessary. Negative rho is minimized by a coherent sign pattern and the 1-direction eigenvalue, giving tau=(1+(n-1)rho)/(1-(n-1)rho). At rho=0 only diagonal entries vary and tau=1. For positive rho the 2-block eigenspace determinant is positive iff u<(K_r-rho)/(K_r+rho), with K_r^2=rho^2+(1-rho)(1+(n-1)rho)/(r(n-r)); balanced group sizes minimize K_r. The other eigenspaces stay positive. Explicit boundary null vectors and indefinite vertices above threshold show sharpness. Even n gives tau=1/cond_2(G); odd n gives a strictly larger radius with the stated n²/(n²-1) limiting ratio. Fresh independent finite sign-vertex calculations checked dimensions 2..8 and correlations of both signs; they corroborate, not prove, the unrestricted symbolic result.
